name: text-0
text:
Alphabet Partitioning
from Interleaved Traces

name: text-1
text: Exact feasibility, certificates, and efficient inference

name: text-2
text: Research progress under explicit assumptions

This presentation separates mathematical guarantees from measurements and open research questions. It does not claim universal recovery of physical devices.

Source: https://github.com/Mahdi-Jadidi/passive-automata-learning/blob/main/results/2026-11-04/scaling_v20/RESEARCH_REPORT_FA.md

name: text-0
text: Research Question

name: text-1
text: Input: positive and negative words over a known alphabet.

name: text-2
text: Infer groups of symbols that can belong to independent components.

name: text-3
text: Determine whether the data imply a unique partition or permit alternatives.

name: text-4
text: The current stage certifies partitions; local DFA learning is separate.

The original motivation is to separate components before passive automata learning. End-to-end RPNI benefits have not been measured.

Source: https://github.com/Mahdi-Jadidi/passive-automata-learning/blob/main/results/2026-11-04/scaling_v20/RESEARCH_REPORT_FA.md

name: text-0
text: Assumptions

name: text-1
text: Every symbol has exactly one owner; the observed alphabet is known.

name: text-2
text: Component languages are regular, with no state-count bound.

name: text-3
text: A global word is accepted exactly when every local projection is accepted.

name: text-4
text: Labels describe complete words and contain no noise.

name: text-5
text: If known K is supplied, it is an externally trusted exact count.

An absent word is not a negative example. Last-event success labels need a different observation model. Synthetic characters encode events; they are not raw event records.

Source: https://github.com/Mahdi-Jadidi/passive-automata-learning/blob/main/results/2026-11-04/preflight_certificates_v19/theory/PREFLIGHT_PROOFS_FA_v1.md

name: text-0
text: Projection onto a Block

name: text-1
text: Projection deletes symbols outside a block and preserves order.

name: text-2
text: For B = {a,b}:   abcd becomes ab;   bacd becomes ba.

name: text-3
text: For B = {a,c}:   both abcd and bacd become ac.

name: text-4
text: A block can distinguish a negative only through its local projection.

The mathematical notation pi(B,w) denotes this projection. This is exact sequence filtering, not similarity clustering.

Source: https://github.com/Mahdi-Jadidi/passive-automata-learning/blob/main/results/2026-11-04/preflight_certificates_v19/theory/PREFLIGHT_PROOFS_FA_v1.md

name: text-0
text: Exact Feasibility Criterion

name: text-1
text: H(B) = { pi(B,p) : p is a positive word }.

name: text-2
text: For every negative n, one block B must distinguish n from every positive.

name: text-3
text: Equivalently: for every n, there exists B with pi(B,n) outside H(B).

name: text-4
text: Necessity: all local positive projections must be accepted.

name: text-5
text: Sufficiency: choose each finite H(B) as its regular witness language.

The quantifier order is for every negative, there exists one block, for every positive. The finite-language witness uses the absence of a local state bound.

Source: https://github.com/Mahdi-Jadidi/passive-automata-learning/blob/main/results/2026-11-04/preflight_certificates_v19/theory/PREFLIGHT_PROOFS_FA_v1.md

name: text-0
text: Example: Unique under Known K

name: text-1
text: Alphabet = {a,b,c,d};  P = {abcd};  N = {bacd, abdc};  K = 2.

name: text-2
text: The first positive/negative pair forces a and b into the same block.

name: text-3
text: The second pair forces c and d into the same block.

name: text-4
text: The forced partition {a,b} / {c,d} is feasible and has exactly K blocks.

name: text-5
text: Therefore this partition is unique under the stated model and K.

If unequal adjacent swapped symbols were in different blocks, every block would see identical projections of the positive and negative. Such a split is impossible.

Source: https://github.com/Mahdi-Jadidi/passive-automata-learning/blob/main/results/2026-11-04/preflight_certificates_v19/theory/PREFLIGHT_PROOFS_FA_v1.md

name: text-0
text: Certificate-Based Precheck

name: text-1
text: Build sound must-link edges; let r be the number of connected components.

name: text-2
text: Every feasible partition must be a coarsening of these forced atoms.

name: text-3
text: If r < K: no compatible K-block partition exists.

name: text-4
text: If r = K: test the only candidate; feasibility proves uniqueness.

name: text-5
text: If 1 < K < r and the atom partition fits: multiple coarsenings fit.

When the atom partition fails and1<K<r, the precheck is undecided and exact search may be needed. KnownK1 is checked directly. r=K alone is not sufficient without feasibility.

Source: https://github.com/Mahdi-Jadidi/passive-automata-learning/blob/main/results/2026-11-04/preflight_certificates_v19/theory/PREFLIGHT_PROOFS_FA_v1.md

name: text-0
text: Meaning of the Four Outcomes

name: text-1
text: Certified unique: exactly one compatible partition, with a completed proof.

name: text-2
text: Ambiguous: two distinct compatible partitions, each with a valid witness.

name: text-3
text: Incompatible: a completed proof that no allowed partition fits.

name: text-4
text: Unresolved: required proof work did not finish within the resource budget.

name: text-5
text: A timeout does not prove data ambiguity or mathematical impossibility.

Only certified_unique releases a selected partition. Unresolved findings leave data_insufficient unknown, rather than asserting insufficiency.

Source: https://github.com/Mahdi-Jadidi/passive-automata-learning/blob/main/results/2026-11-04/scaling_v20/RESEARCH_REPORT_FA.md

name: text-0
text: Current Exact Algorithm

name: text-1
text: Validate input and labels; apply exact count-based shortcuts.

name: text-2
text: Discover forced atoms and check their projected positive/negative data.

name: text-3
text: If necessary, search canonical coarsenings without duplicate partitions.

name: text-4
text: Use bounded caches and safe block-count pruning.

name: text-5
text: Stop with a proof, two witnesses, or an explicit unresolved result.

This decision gate stops after two compatible witnesses; it does not enumerate the whole output family. Small complete-family solvers remain independent correctness references.

Source: https://github.com/Mahdi-Jadidi/passive-automata-learning/blob/main/results/2026-11-04/scaling_v20/RESEARCH_REPORT_FA.md

name: text-0
text: Previously Audited Exact Speedups

name: text-1
text: Parikh filtering: adjacent swaps require equal length and symbol counts.

name: text-2
text: Only matching pairs enter the unchanged exact swap verifier.

name: text-3
text: Native projection: delete all symbols outside a block in bounded chunks.

name: text-4
text: All input is validated before applying native string translation.

name: text-5
text: These changes preserve feasible partitions; they do not remove worst-case search.

These are C020 C1 and C2. Hash equality alone never establishes a constraint; Python dictionaries resolve full exact key equality.

Source: https://github.com/Mahdi-Jadidi/passive-automata-learning/blob/main/results/2026-11-04/scaling_v20/RESEARCH_REPORT_FA.md

name: text-0
text: New Exact Improvement: Witness Transfer

name: text-1
text: Precondition: the forced-atom partition has already passed exact validation.

name: text-2
text: For each negative, retain an atom that rejects its local projection.

name: text-3
text: In a coarsening, map that rejection to the block containing the entire atom.

name: text-4
text: Equality on the larger block would imply equality on the rejecting atom.

name: text-5
text: Therefore coarsened witnesses can be constructed without scanning traces again.

The transfer is invalid if an atom is split or the atom partition was never verified. It changes rejecting-block choices and work counters, not completed feasibility semantics. It does not affect unique, unary, or DFS routes.

Source: https://github.com/Mahdi-Jadidi/passive-automata-learning/blob/main/results/2026-11-04/partition_transfer_v22/theory/TRANSFER_PROOF_V1.md

name: text-0
text: Evaluation Design

name: text-1
text: C020 used four fixed inputs and six timing configurations.

name: text-2
text: The largest input has 20 minimal 1024-state devices and 32,338,004 characters.

name: text-3
text: Sampling is conditioned; informative swap witnesses are deliberately planted.

name: text-4
text: The new candidate is compared on the same saved inputs and fixed count controls.

name: text-5
text: Every result needs independent witness checks; timing includes reading and preprocessing.

LowerK coarsening controls measure mathematical ambiguity under declared count constraints; they are not recovery tests with the generator's physical device count. No hidden ownership or DFA tables are solver inputs.

Source: https://github.com/Mahdi-Jadidi/passive-automata-learning/blob/main/results/2026-11-04/scaling_v20/RESEARCH_REPORT_FA.md
Source: https://github.com/Mahdi-Jadidi/passive-automata-learning/blob/main/results/2026-11-04/partition_transfer_v22/theory/TRANSFER_PROOF_V1.md

name: text-0
text: Established C020 Measurements

name: text-1
text: A, known K=4: median end-to-end time fell from 6.403 s to 0.658 s.

name: text-2
text: B, known K=8: C2 completed in 3.174 s; baseline did not finish in 20 s.

name: text-3
text: C, unknown K: C2 certified ambiguity in 7.942 s; baseline was unresolved.

name: text-4
text: A separate single K=20 control certified uniqueness in 5.284 s.

name: text-5
text: Small control D became 19.9% slower end-to-end; universal speed dominance is not claimed.

The main table uses medians of three fresh processes. The K20 functional control is one separate run. No finite speed ratio is assigned where the baseline was censored. These are not real-world recovery accuracy figures.

Source: https://github.com/Mahdi-Jadidi/passive-automata-learning/blob/main/results/2026-11-04/scaling_v20/RESEARCH_REPORT_FA.md

name: text-0
text: New Candidate: Evaluation Boundary

name: text-1
text: The new optimization targets ambiguity after compatible forced atoms.

name: text-2
text: Only coarsened-witness replay is replaced; exact search is unchanged.

name: text-3
text: The same inputs, count constraints, budgets, and output requirements apply.

name: text-4
text: Performance and independent-correctness results accompany this presentation.

Only measured completed comparisons can support numeric ratios. A proof of soundness alone is not evidence of a speedup.

Source: https://github.com/Mahdi-Jadidi/passive-automata-learning/blob/main/results/2026-11-04/partition_transfer_v22/theory/TRANSFER_PROOF_V1.md

name: text-0
text: Complexity and Remaining Limits

name: text-1
text: Reading the input requires work proportional to its total size.

name: text-2
text: Equal Parikh signatures can retain every positive/negative comparison.

name: text-3
text: Potential atom partitions number Bell(r), or S(r,K) at fixed K.

name: text-4
text: Worst-case exact search remains combinatorial.

name: text-5
text: More hidden DFA states do not by themselves imply harder observed inference.

Bell and Stirling values count possible partitions, not exact complete runtime. Transfer removes redundant replay on one proved route; it does not strengthen identifiability or improve every path.

Source: https://github.com/Mahdi-Jadidi/passive-automata-learning/blob/main/results/2026-11-04/scaling_v20/RESEARCH_REPORT_FA.md
Source: https://github.com/Mahdi-Jadidi/passive-automata-learning/blob/main/results/2026-11-04/partition_transfer_v22/theory/TRANSFER_PROOF_V1.md

name: text-1

name: text-2

name: text-3
text: End-to-end benefits for RPNI remain unmeasured.

name: text-4

name: text-5

The LANCER real-data goal remains paused at the user's request. No claim of universal physical ownership recovery is made.

name: text-0
text: Backup: Quantifier Counterexample

name: text-1
text: P = {bacd, abdc};  N = {abcd};  K = 2.

name: text-2
text: Swaps force the only candidate {a,b} / {c,d}.

name: text-3
text: On {a,b}, the negative matches positive abdc.

name: text-4
text: On {c,d}, it matches positive bacd.

name: text-5
text: No single block rejects the negative against all positives; the sample is incompatible.

For every positive, a different block distinguishing it is insufficient. The correct order is for every negative, there exists one block, for every positive.

Source: https://github.com/Mahdi-Jadidi/passive-automata-learning/blob/main/results/2026-11-04/preflight_certificates_v19/theory/PREFLIGHT_PROOFS_FA_v1.md

name: text-0
text: Backup: Identifiability Limits

name: text-1
text: Without known K, a consistent finite sample always has a one-block explanation.

name: text-2
text: If a multi-block explanation also fits, the architecture is ambiguous.

name: text-3
text: Counts alone do not guarantee uniqueness: even/odd a-count samples fit every partition.

name: text-4
text: Known K can enable certificates, but arbitrary samples with that K may remain ambiguous.

UnknownK is not always ambiguous: a sample may uniquely force one block. No general finite count or maximum-length threshold guarantees multicomponent recovery under unbounded regular factors.

Source: https://github.com/Mahdi-Jadidi/passive-automata-learning/blob/main/results/2026-11-04/preflight_certificates_v19/theory/PREFLIGHT_PROOFS_FA_v1.md

name: text-0
text: Selected References

name: text-1
text: Oncina and Garcia (1992): passive DFA inference.

name: text-2
text: Gold (1967): language identification in the limit.

name: text-3
text: Angluin (1987): learning from queries and counterexamples.

name: text-4
text: Jecker, Mazzocchi, and Wolf (2021): permutation automata decomposition.

name: text-5
text: These sources provide context, not a completed novelty review.

Inferring Regular Languages in Polynomial Updated Time
https://doi.org/10.1142/9789812797902_0004
Introduces the RPNI passive state-merging context for inferring a DFA consistent with positive and negative examples; this project instead reasons over ownership partitions and does not learn component DFAs.

Language identification in the limit
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0019995867911655
Foundational identification-in-the-limit results distinguish positive-only text from labeled informants and motivate why finite observations require explicit assumptions and coverage conditions; it is not a direct theorem about this partition solver.

Learning Regular Sets from Queries and Counterexamples
https://homepages.math.uic.edu/~lreyzin/papers/angluin87.pdf
Defines the active teacher/query setting for regular-language learning, useful as a contrast with the static labeled sample here; the paper's oracle access is not assumed by this project.

Decomposing Permutation Automata
https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.CONCUR.2021.18
Studies decomposition of a given DFA language into intersections of smaller DFA languages, a neighboring compositionality problem; its input, decomposition target, and hypotheses differ from inferring a disjoint alphabet partition from positive/negative words.
